indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.3.1 Demonstrate an understanding of a metre and centimetre (cm, m) units for measuring length
indicator.objective: Model and describe the relationship between the units metre and centimetre

skills.description: Identify objects measuring about 1 cm or 1 m.
Measure and record lengths using a ruler.
Draw a line segment of a given length.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Starting measurement from the 1 mark instead of 0.
Drawing lines without using a ruler.

questions.stem: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
Which object is about 1 metre long?
hints: 1 metre is about the height of a door handle.
questions.explanation: A door is about 1 metre long.

questions.stem: Which object is about 1 cm long?
How many centimetres in 2 metres?
Convert 3 metres to centimetres.
How many metres is 500 cm?
When measuring a line with a ruler, where should you place the 0 mark?
options: At the start of the line
At the end of the line
In the middle of the line
questions.explanation: Place the 0 mark at the start of the line.

questions.stem: A pencil starts at 0 cm and ends at 12 cm on a ruler. How long is it?
A line starts at 3 cm and ends at 10 cm on a ruler. How long is it?
Convert 450 cm to metres.
Which is longer: 150 cm or 1 m?
Draw a line segment that is 8 cm long.
Draw a line segment that is 4 cm long.

criteria.description: Draws a line exactly 4 cm long.

questions.stem: Two lines are measured. Line A is 15 cm. Line B is 8 cm. What is the difference in length?
Explain how to measure a line segment using a ruler.
hints: Read the number at the end.
questions.explanation: Place the ruler with the 0 mark at one end of the line. Read the number at the other end. The difference is the length.

questions.stem: How many centimetres are in 1.5 metres?
A pupil measures a table as 120 cm. Another measures it as 1.2 m. Are they both correct? Explain.
questions.explanation: Yes, they are both correct. 1.2 m = 120 cm.

questions.stem: Draw a line segment of 12 cm.

criteria.description: Draws a line exactly 12 cm long.

questions.stem: A pupil measures a line from 2 cm to 9 cm and says it is 9 cm long. Explain their mistake.
questions.explanation: The pupil read the end mark (9) instead of the length. They should subtract the start from the end: 9 - 2 = 7 cm.
questions.misconception: Thinking the end number is always the length.

questions.stem: A rope is 2.5 m long. How many cm is it?

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.2.1 Demonstrate that the length of an object does not change with its placement or direction
indicator.objective: Represent whole numbers as distances from any given location on a number line.

skills.description: Find the distance between two points on a number line.
Place a rod on different number points and count the unit intervals it covers.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.

questions.stem: How many units are between 0 and 5 on a number line?
A stick is placed from 2 to 5 on a number line. How long is the stick?
questions.misconception: Saying 5 because the end is at 5.

questions.stem: How many units between 10 and 15?
If a worm starts at 3 and moves to 8, how many units did it travel?
A line segment goes from 0 to 4. What is its length?
A stick covers the distance from 4 to 11. How many units is that?
If a rod of length 5 is placed starting at 3, where does it end?
A rope is placed on a number line from 2 to 9. Explain how to find its length.
questions.explanation: Subtract the starting point from the ending point: 9 - 2 = 7 units.

questions.stem: How far is it from 6 to 20 on a number line?
A rod of length 8 starts at 5. Where does it end?
A pupil places a 4-unit rod at 0. They move it to start at 3. What is the new ending point?
questions.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7. (The length didn't change, just the location).
questions.misconception: Saying 4 because the rod is length 4.

questions.stem: A pupil walks from 12 to 25. How far did they walk?
Explain why the length of a stick doesn't change when you move it on a number line.
hints: Does the distance between the ends change?
questions.explanation: The distance between the endpoints of the stick remains the same regardless of where it is placed on the number line. It's the same stick.

criteria.description: States the length is the same.
Explains the distance between ends is constant.

questions.misconception: Thinking moving it changes the length.

questions.stem: How many units from 15 to 42?
Describe how to place a 6-unit rod on a number line starting at 4.
questions.explanation: Start at 4 and count 6 units to the right: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. The rod ends at 10.

questions.stem: A number line has marks at 0, 5, 10, 15... What is the distance between the 2nd and 5th mark?
A stick of length 7 is placed on a number line ending at 12. Where does it start?
Two sticks are placed on a number line. Stick A goes from 2 to 9. Stick B goes from 15 to 22. Which is longer? Explain.
questions.explanation: Both are the same length (7 units).
questions.misconception: Saying B is longer because it ends at a larger number.

questions.stem: A pupil walks from 3 to 18. They take a break at 10. How much further do they have to walk?

indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.1.1 Analyse the relationships among and between 2-D shapes and 3-D objects according to a variety of attributes, including measurement
indicator.objective: Use attributes to recognize rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories

skills.description: Recognize and name rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids, rectangles, and squares.
Draw quadrilaterals that do not belong to the named subcategories.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking a square is not a rectangle.
Confusing a rhombus with a square.

questions.stem: Which of these is a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral.
questions.misconception: Saying a triangle is a quadrilateral.

questions.stem: A rectangle has how many sides?
hints: Count the sides of a rectangle.

questions.stem: Which shape is a quadrilateral with all sides equal but no right angles?
questions.explanation: A rhombus has all sides equal but angles are not 90 degrees.

questions.stem: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
hints: Parallel means lines that never meet.
questions.explanation: A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides.

questions.stem: How many sides does a parallelogram have?
Which statement is true?
hints: A square has all the properties of a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A square is a special rectangle with equal sides.

questions.stem: A shape has 4 sides, opposite sides are equal, and all angles are right angles. What is it?
hints: It could be a square, but square is a type of rectangle. Let's look for the general name.
questions.misconception: Saying square (a square is a specific type, but 'rectangle' is the broader category that fits all those properties).

questions.stem: Draw a quadrilateral that is NOT a square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, or trapezoid.
hints: Make the sides unequal and with no parallel lines.
questions.explanation: An irregular quadrilateral with no parallel sides.

criteria.description: Does not fit any of the named categories.

questions.stem: What is the name of a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides and 4 right angles?
hints: All sides equal, all corners square.
questions.misconception: Saying rhombus (which doesn't have right angles).

questions.stem: A parallelogram has how many pairs of parallel sides?
Explain why a square is also a rectangle.
hints: What are the properties of a rectangle?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides that are equal, which are the exact properties of a rectangle.
questions.misconception: Thinking squares and rectangles are mutually exclusive.

questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a trapezoid have?
Which of these is a special type of parallelogram?
hints: A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides.
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all sides equal.

questions.stem: Compare a square and a rhombus. How are they alike and how are they different?
questions.explanation: Alike: Both have 4 equal sides. Different: A square has 4 right angles, while a rhombus may not.

criteria.description: States square has right angles, rhombus may not.

questions.misconception: Thinking they are the same shape.

questions.stem: Draw a trapezoid.
questions.explanation: Any 4-sided shape with exactly one pair of parallel sides.

criteria.description: Draws a shape with exactly one pair of parallel sides.

questions.stem: Which statement is FALSE?
hints: A rectangle doesn't have to have equal sides.
questions.explanation: Not all rectangles are squares (sides can be different lengths).

questions.stem: Explain the hierarchy of quadrilaterals. Start with quadrilateral and branch out.
questions.explanation: All squares are rectangles, all rectangles are parallelograms, and all parallelograms are quadrilaterals.

criteria.description: Correctly shows the relationships between the subcategories.

questions.misconception: Thinking the categories are completely separate.

questions.stem: Draw a rhombus that is not a square.
questions.explanation: A slanted shape with 4 equal sides.

criteria.description: Draws a shape with 4 equal sides.
The shape does not have right angles.

questions.stem: A shape has 4 sides and 2 pairs of parallel sides. What are three possible names for this shape?
hints: Think of parallelograms, rectangles, and squares.

criteria.description: Gives at least two valid names.
